claims.claim: ⚠️ **The Sydney funnel-web can cause lethal envenoming**, although Victoria has no recorded case of severe envenoming, even though some local spiders are of similar toxicity.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Spider Bite - Big Black Spider' (Last Updated August, 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Spider_Bite_-_Big_Black_Spider/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The Victorian funnel-web (Dandenong Ranges) is not significantly venomous** — bite-site pain, headache, nausea. **Beware collectors' Sydney funnel-webs**; other funnel-webs and mouse spiders reaching eastern Victoria may cause systemic symptoms.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Spider Bite - Big Black Spider' (Last Updated August, 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Spider_Bite_-_Big_Black_Spider/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Apart from redbacks, other Victorian spiders need no medical intervention or observation unless infection develops.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Spider Bite - Big Black Spider' (Last Updated August, 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Spider_Bite_-_Big_Black_Spider/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Assess anyone in whom a Sydney funnel-web bite is possible, and any symptomatic patient.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Spider Bite - Big Black Spider' (Last Updated August, 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Spider_Bite_-_Big_Black_Spider/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Only a small number of bites cause systemic envenoming; if it comes, it develops over 10 minutes to 4 hours.** Bite marks are usually seen.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Spider Bite - Big Black Spider' (Last Updated August, 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Spider_Bite_-_Big_Black_Spider/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Systemic features:** tingling around the mouth · abdominal pain, headache, nausea, vomiting · salivation, piloerection, sweating, lacrimation · hypertension and tachycardia, possibly followed by bradycardia and hypotension · cyanosis, pulmonary oedema, respiratory failure.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Spider Bite - Big Black Spider' (Last Updated August, 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Spider_Bite_-_Big_Black_Spider/, retrieved 2026-09-23

The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Spider Bite - Big Black Spider' (Last Updated August, 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Spider_Bite_-_Big_Black_Spider/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Put on a pressure immobilisation bandage.** Where the history or examination points to envenoming, **keep it in place** and talk to the Poisons Information Centre.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Spider Bite - Big Black Spider' (Last Updated August, 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Spider_Bite_-_Big_Black_Spider/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **No Victorian hospital stocks Sydney funnel-web antivenom** — contact the Poisons Information Centre. If the child has symptoms or a Sydney funnel-web cannot be excluded, **have 4 ampoules of the CSL antivenom for funnel-web spider on hand before the bandage comes off.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Spider Bite - Big Black Spider' (Last Updated August, 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Spider_Bite_-_Big_Black_Spider/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Without antivenom, support organ by organ:** intubation with IPPV/PEEP for pulmonary oedema · alpha blockade for tachycardia and hypertension · hypotension — fluids, inotropes, atropine.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Spider Bite - Big Black Spider' (Last Updated August, 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Spider_Bite_-_Big_Black_Spider/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Possible Sydney funnel-web, or any symptoms: discharge only if asymptomatic 4 hours after the bite and at least 2 hours after first aid is removed.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Spider Bite - Big Black Spider' (Last Updated August, 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Spider_Bite_-_Big_Black_Spider/, retrieved 2026-09-23
